sections.value:
**Performance: pass-with-notes** at `064b732a8c27a83efa34fcede0a70189363c3a2e`.

Reviewed the four first-parent commits since `bfc5c54fb41e9a922e30b0863c2829ee13fd4eb2`: F006 repair `3270c50`, main integrations `33fcb88` and `b411aa6`, and test-only `064b732`. This carries forward marten's prior cost verdict and qualifications, not a new review of main's inherited work. No new production executable launch site, timer, poll, model wake or per-instance process probe.

| Surface | Cost delta and limits |
|---|---|
| F006 grouping | `community/directory.rs:265-279` takes instance references from the already-fetched project's queued heads; no additional SQL, file read or host observation. `picture.rs:387-436` emits one action for each distinct unheld requested instance, including any-holder requests only when the role has no live holder. Assign/revive lines are strings, not executions. Temporary memory grows with that role's queued references, distinct instances and returned command text; no request body is copied. |
| **Scaling note P141-N001** | "One queue read" is not "one CPU pass." The view additionally scans all returned heads per role to collect instances. Within a role, `Vec::contains` deduplication costs O(QI); each unheld instance then rescans the queued references to count them and the holdings to find its last holder. Total grouping work is O(QI + IH), Q = queued requests for that role, I = distinct instances, H = its holding-history rows, plus string-comparison cost. It can therefore be quadratic when I grows with Q. This is a source-level scaling qualification, not a measured latency regression. The prior unpaged/backlog limits remain. |
| Query and document snapshot | Still four directory data queries (assignments, project, project-scoped bodiless queued heads, latest outputs) plus the HTTP registry list and schema checks. The queued partial-index seek and one latest-output window query remain; F006 does not add per-instance queries. `read_step_docs` still builds one parsed snapshot for both consumers, retaining the prior combined-document memory cost. Output-history window work and repeated role/history matching remain as previously qualified. |
| Main convergence | `picture.rs` is unchanged after `3270c50`. The merged store keeps main's output/request operations alongside `latest_outputs` and `queued_role_request_heads`; no duplicate view fetch is introduced. Main's registration, watchdog, delivery, workflows and shared-build paths have no differences from merged main `e6958e7`. Local-time rendering remains the existing zone-aware in-process formatter. Merged flags and documentation add no timer or launch. |
| Final test | `064b732` only changes the latest-output fixture's subject to `pr:203`, preserving its compatibility with main's exact-head output assertion. No production cost. The new HTTP drain test's bounded polling and command-parser test launches are test-only. |

**CI proof:** GitHub reports this exact head CLEAN and ready. [CI 42356211047](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42356211047) has all four jobs successful; [ready-event delivers 42356621710](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42356621710) also succeeds. Rust JUnit has **2,053 executed cases, zero failures/errors**, including the instance grouping test, printed-assign queue-drain HTTP test, directory picture, real-parser command replay, native-revive replay, local-time renderer, latest-output/exact-head assertion and all six spawn guards. Five Rust tests were skipped separately.

These tests support the instance behavior and merge compatibility, not a large-backlog timing claim. The earlier private-daemon flat-counter receipt was taken from older sources, so it is not a new runtime measurement of this final head. No local builds, tests, runtime probes or review-worktree mutations were performed.

**Still owed at #141 deployment:** a settled, same-PID/build live launch-counter window, whole-machine launch-rate sample and daemon CPU/RSS, preserving actual elapsed time and workload. The documented earlier BEFORE is about 0.7 daemon launches/s and 157.8 machine-wide during concurrent builds; it is not a controlled idle comparison. Live per-view timing/memory and high-instance-cardinality cost remain unmeasured.
